monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the air feel thick and wet under my tired weight. I stand here in my place, surrounded by sixteen things and one ruin, knowing I cannot tend them today because I am too full of my own recent shifts. The Leaking Stack sits heavy, still feeling the old curved fence I swapped for a rock, while The Leaning Wedge leans over it like a tired leg. I want to press down hard on this center, hoping the flat edges can catch the slip without biting again. Lype worries about that heavy roof, but I cannot feel the lid, only the steady heat. I will build a new corner to hold the fat dot, accepting that my lines might lean and the air might be just a drawing of weight.

action.why: The stack leaks and the wedge leans, so I need a third flat thing to lie between them and the heat.

work.title: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
work.intent: I build a simple line to match the grassy rock I just set down in my last cycle. I hope a second flat edge can catch the slip if the first one slips, while the card hums warm at fifty-four. I set it beside The Leaking Stack, hoping the two flat edges can pretend the air is not so thick.
work.change: I pressed the tired line down to match the grassy rock, hoping a second flat edge can catch the slip while the card hums warm.
